about.title: About Paxl
about.subtitle: A visual landing page editor built as a personal project.
about.missionBody: Paxl is a block-based landing page editor. It is a complete project from end to end: an editor with a lot of state in the browser, its own API, real-time collaboration and AI generation that returns valid blocks instead of free text.
about.authorBody: David Palmero, web developer. The code is public and the architecture decisions are documented in the repository.
about.principle1Body: Every block has defined fields. It gives less freedom than a blank canvas, but the page doesn't fall apart and AI can generate blocks that fit.
about.principle2Body: Colors, fonts and spacing are chosen once for the whole page and blocks inherit them. Switching palettes changes the whole page at once.
about.principle3Body: Changes reach the server a few seconds after you make them. No need to remember to save.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Paxl is the demo of a personal project. This page explains, plainly, what data the app stores today. I recommend not using real personal data: a test name and email are enough.
privacy.section1Body: Your username, your email and your password (stored as a hash). If you sign in with Google, also your Google identifier, name and picture. And, of course, the pages you create, their versions and the images you upload.
privacy.section2Body: Analytics on published pages uses no cookies and stores nothing on the visitor's device. It records the page path (without URL parameters), the origin of the referring site, UTM tags, screen size, the block clicked and where its links point, and an anonymous identifier the server computes from the IP and browser with a key that changes every day. The IP and browser are not stored, and the identifier cannot recognise a person across different days. If a visitor sends a page's contact form, their name, email and message are stored for the page author to read; the IP is not stored.
privacy.section3Body: Two cookies keep you signed in (bp_access and bp_refresh), and they exist only if you sign in or start a guest session. Another cookie, paxl-locale, remembers the language only when you change it with the switcher; if you never touch it, the app uses your browser's language and stores nothing. The browser's local storage keeps your light or dark theme preference (when you change it) and a backup of the page you are editing, so a network failure does not lose your changes. Published pages set no cookies and store nothing on the device of whoever visits them.
privacy.section4Body: If you use AI generation, your instruction and the block content are sent to Google (Gemini) or Anthropic. If you use your own key, it is only used for that request and is not stored. Sign-in with Google loads Google's script only on the sign-in and sign-up screens, and only if the server has that sign-in configured: published pages and the rest of the app never contact Google. If you sign in with Google, Google knows you signed in here. Payments are turned off in the demo; if they are turned on, they go through Stripe in test mode: nothing is charged and no real card is needed.
privacy.section5Body: Data is not sold or used for advertising. It is only used to make the app work.
privacy.section6Body: You can delete your account yourself from Settings, under Delete account (it asks for your password or for you to type your username). Your account, your pages and their versions, the messages received through forms, the analytics and the images you uploaded are permanently deleted. If you have an active paid subscription, it has to be cancelled first. Guest accounts delete themselves after 24 hours. If something goes wrong, write to me through davidpalmero.dev.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: Short terms for using the Paxl demo.
terms.section1Body: Paxl is offered as is, as a personal project. It may change, break or go offline without notice, and data may be lost. Don't use it for anything important.
terms.section2Body: Don't publish illegal or misleading content, or content that infringes other people's rights. Pages or accounts that do may be removed.
terms.section3Body: Payments are turned off in this demo. If they are turned on, they run in Stripe's test mode: nothing is charged and no real card is needed.
terms.section4Body: What you create in Paxl is yours. It is only used to show your pages.

changelog.title: Changelog
changelog.subtitle: What has changed in Paxl, taken from the repository history.
changelog.entry1Body: Continuous integration and pinned dependencies. Light mode fixed and AA contrast in both modes. The dashboard shows the real plan and the editor canvas centers itself. Published pages keep their template theme.
changelog.entry2Body: Django backend with accounts, pages, versions, analytics, billing and real-time collaboration. Pages dashboard, publishing, server autosave and a mobile editor.
changelog.entry3Body: Visual editor with blocks, a properties inspector, drag and drop, undo and redo. Pages were saved in the browser.
